chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ali b. Shu'ayb al-Jawhari (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr b. Abdullah b. Habib narrated to us. He said: al-Fadl b. al-Saqr al-Abdi narrated to us. He said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us from al-A'mash from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:
The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) went out wearing a khamisa, having wrapped himself in it. So it was said: O Messenger of Allah, who clothed you in this khamisa?

He said: My beloved and my elect, my special one and my pure one, the one who fulfills on my behalf, my deputy, my inheritor, and my brother; the first of the believers to embrace Islam, the sincerest of them in faith, and the most generous of people in giving; the Master of the people after me, the Leader of the shining radiant believers, the Imam of the people of the Earth — Ali b. Abi Talib clothed me in it.
Then he did not cease weeping until the pebbles became wet from his tears, out of longing for him.

key_terms.الغر المحجلين: Literally 'the white-faced and white-limbed ones,' this term refers to believers who will be recognized on the Day of Judgment by the light of their wudu (ablution), radiating from their faces and limbs
key_terms.خميصة: A khamisa is a black bordered garment, typically a cloak or shawl with decorated edges, worn as an outer wrap
key_terms.سيد الناس بعدي: Master of the people after me — a designation of supreme authority and leadership after the Prophet
key_terms.وصيي: Wasi (deputy/executor) — a term denoting the appointed successor who carries out the will and mission of the Prophet; a key term in Shia theology regarding Imam Ali's appointment

ai.seo_question: What titles did the Prophet Muhammad give to Ali ibn Abi Talib when praising him about the cloak (khamisa)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) publicly praises Ali b. Abi Talib (AS) with a series of extraordinary titles while wearing a cloak that Ali had given him. The hadith is significant because it demonstrates the Prophet's open expression of Ali's status as his chosen successor, using titles such as 'my deputy' (wasi), 'my inheritor' (warith), and 'Master of the people after me' — language that carries strong implications of religious and political succession in the Islamic context. The Prophet's tears of longing for Ali, despite Ali being alive, suggest a deep spiritual dimension to their bond that early audiences would have understood as evidence of Ali's exalted station.
